selected_gap.title: Daily hyperlocal predictive fishing maps via accessible channel
selected_gap.pain: Artisanal fishermen waste 40–60% of fuel costs searching for fish, relying on traditional methods, generic quarterly bulletins, or expensive reactive hardware. No existing solution delivers daily, species‑specific predictions tailored to their exact fishing zones through a low‑barrier channel like WhatsApp.
selected_gap.why_now: Free satellite data (NASA, Copernicus) + cheap cloud computing enable scalable processing. WhatsApp penetration is high among fishing communities, and cooperatives seek fuel savings amid rising prices. Competitors are either industrial‑focused or lack predictive features.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Pilot with 50 vessels from 3 cooperatives: measure fuel consumption reduction and catch rate change vs control group; interview cooperative managers on willingness to pay per vessel per year.
selected_gap.risk: Initial prediction inaccuracy could damage trust; government might eventually offer a free alternative; regulatory closures may limit actual fishing zones.

idea: PescaIA pivots to serve seafood export companies in Peru who are dependent on artisanal fishermen for their supply. These companies bear the hidden cost of supply unpredictability caused by fishermen wasting 40-60% of their fuel searching blindly for fish. PescaIA sells a predictive intelligence platform directly to the exporter, who then provides the daily WhatsApp catch maps to their network of fishermen for free. This creates a sticky supply chain: fishermen get better catches and lower fuel costs, while the exporter gains real-time visibility into expected landings, reduces procurement risk, and secures higher compliance with international contracts. Revenue comes from annual enterprise licenses based on the number of vessels served, with premium features like supply forecasting dashboards for the buyer.

idea: Focus exclusively on predicting daily aggregation zones for jumbo flying squid (pota) for a single artisanal fishing cooperative in Paita, Peru. Using free NASA satellite data (SST, chlorophyll) and simple behavioral rules for pota, we manually generate a heatmap image each morning and send it via WhatsApp to the cooperative’s 10–15 boat captains. The wedge is hyper-local, single-species, single-cooperative, delivered through the channel they already use, with the sole goal of demonstrating immediate fuel savings and securing a paid pilot within 30 days.
